summary: Full M1 (identity/org/facility/role/approval/auth) verification against the external preview URL. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_m1_live_api.py (29 live cookie-based API tests) covering unauthenticated 401s, hospital/supplier registration -> PENDING, org_pending 403 gating, cross-org 403 isolation, non-admin 403 on approve/list, admin approval + invalid transition 409, suspend -> org_suspended 403, logout/refresh, HttpOnly+Secure cookie flags, bcrypt $2b$ hash in DB, profile PATCH persistence, and brute-force 429 lockout. Frontend: two Playwright runs covering role select -> login (client validation, invalid creds toast, Google redirect URL), hospital + supplier registration -> status-pending, sign out -> /auth/me 401, unauthenticated /app redirect, admin login -> app-shell-admin, approval via admin session, approved hospital/supplier -> app-shell-hospital/app-shell-supplier, profile view+update, suspended -> status-suspended, and login lockout message after 6 failures. Full suite: 47/47 pytest passing; all frontend assertions passed. No functional defects found; 1 medium security/robustness concern on rate-limit keying.

minor.issue: Throttle key is the client IP derived from the first X-Forwarded-For hop. Behind the preview ingress ALL traffic shares one IP (observed rate_events identifier 'register:34.170.12.145'), so the 20/hour cap is effectively global and returns 429 to legitimate new organisations. Also, because X-Forwarded-For is caller-supplied, an attacker can rotate the header to bypass both the register throttle and the login lockout identifier (ip:email). Recommend trusting only the proxy-verified client IP (or keying login lockout on email alone) and raising/segmenting the register limit.
Approval/suspension is API-only — there is no admin approval UI in the M1 admin shell, so an admin cannot approve a PENDING organisation from the product itself. Confirm this is intentional for M1.

issues: Greeting renders 'Welcome, CARE-E.' because it takes the first token of full_name 'CARE-E Administrator' — cosmetic wording nit
Admin header shows organisation placeholder 'CARE-E Network' (admin has no organisation) — acceptable but reads like real data

Two 401 console errors on every unauthenticated page load from the initial GET /auth/me session probe — expected behaviour, but noisy; could be silenced by treating 401 as a normal unauthenticated response

action_items: Decide on rate-limit keying: shared-ingress IP makes the 20/hour registration cap global, and X-Forwarded-For is spoofable so login lockout (ip:email) can be bypassed.
Confirm whether an admin approval UI is expected in M1 (currently approvals are only possible via PATCH /api/v1/organisations/{id}).
critical_code_review_comments: core/rate_limit.py + api/v1/auth.py: _client_ip() trusts the first X-Forwarded-For value, which is client-controlled. Derive the IP from a trusted proxy hop count, or key brute-force lockout on the email only.

services/auth_service.py google_complete(): calls register_hospital/register_supplier with password='' (bcrypt-hashes an empty string) then nulls password_hash; safe today but fragile — pass a provider flag instead of a placeholder password.

services/auth_service.py: _ensure_email_free() + create is a check-then-act race; the unique index on users.email (migration_0002) is what actually protects it, and the compensating cleanup relies on that. Worth an explicit comment/duplicate-key catch.

Google login path (google_login_or_onboard) logs in any existing user matching the Google email without verifying that the account was provisioned for Google — an account created with password auth can be taken over by whoever controls that Google address. Consider requiring authentication_provider match or explicit linking.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_m1_live_api.py for regression (hits the external REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL with cookie sessions; module-scoped fixtures register fresh unique orgs per xdist worker). rca_of_the_issue: No product defects reproduced. Earlier suite failures were caused by the register rate limiter: the in-process TestClient suite shares identifier 'register:testclient' and live tests share the ingress IP bucket, so consecutive runs hit 429 and registration-dependent tests failed. Fixed test-side (skip on 429 + session-scoped throttle-counter reset); the underlying shared-IP keying is reported as a product concern.
